researcher_notes: RWE publicly announced the Brunsbüttel green-ammonia import terminal on 18 March 2022 (first public proposal); deliveries planned from 2026. Phase 1 = the initial import facility. Confirmed by RWE's own press release (primary) plus three independent outlets (pipeline-journal, Ammonia Energy Association, safety4sea), all carrying 2022 + ammonia/Brunsbüttel. (RWE press release is published in English.)

Same 18 March 2022 RWE announcement. Phase 2 = the planned expansion of the Brunsbüttel ammonia import terminal beyond the initial Phase-1 capacity; GEM models the terminal as Phase 1/Phase 2 units, both originating in the 2022 proposal. Proposal year 2022 per the same set of independent sources (all carrying 2022 + ammonia/Brunsbüttel).

The NWO (Nord-West Oelleitung) 9 bcm/y FSRU proposal at Wilhelmshaven emerged March 2022 (Lower Saxony minister Olaf Lies floated commissioning by autumn 2023) but stalled with no formal shelving announcement. GEM substatus 'inferred 2 y' implies the shelved year is GEM's inference year (~2024; last real activity 2022). No independent source dating a specific shelving event was verifiable before the session web-tool limit. UNRESOLVED; unverified candidate years: 2024 (inferred) or 2022 (last activity).

The Ceylon Electricity Board floated the international tender for the offshore Kerawalapitiya FSRU/LNG import terminal in February 2021 — the first public proposal of this FSRU terminal. Verified via Upstream (2021 + Kerawalapitiya). Single on-point verified source (economynext/energyvoice/lngjournal returned 403/403/403), so medium tier. Caveat: this is timeline entry order 6 and may correspond to a later re-tender/re-proposal (Petronet 2021 -> Engro 2022 -> CHEC 2025); 2021 is the first public proposal per the brief's status mapping. Two other URLs passed the verifier (maritime.direct, sundaytimes) but were excluded as they concern the separate New Fortress Colombo terminal and the 2018 Kerawalapitiya power-plant tender respectively, not this FSRU terminal proposal.

New Fortress Energy signed a definitive agreement with Sri Lanka in Sept 2021 (40% Yugadanavi stake + an offshore Colombo LNG receiving terminal). The unsolicited deal was never implemented amid strong objections; the government shifted toward other developers (Petronet/Engro) through 2022-2023, and NFE itself entered financial distress in 2024-2025. No source explicitly dating a formal cancellation/termination was verifiable before the session web-tool limit. UNRESOLVED; unverified candidate year ~2023 (government abandonment of the NFE proposal) or 2024.

terminal: SK Group Sri Lanka LNG Terminal
researcher_notes: SK Group announced a ~US$600m Sri Lanka LNG project in July 2020 (BOOT, to supply 930 MW of power plants). No development updates since; GEM substatus 'inferred 4 y' implies cancelled at the inference year (~2024); last real activity 2020. There was no formal cancellation event and no sourceable cancellation year. UNRESOLVED (could not verify a cancellation-year source before the session web-tool limit).

The Chana (Songkhla) industrial-estate scheme — including the LNG terminal + LNG-fired power plant (KOWEPO/TPIPP/KOGAS MOU, March 2021) — was halted by a Thai cabinet resolution on 14 Dec 2021 pending a Strategic Environmental Assessment, after major protests; the project never resumed and GEM later inferred it cancelled ('inferred 4 y'). 2021 is the effective-abandonment/last-activity year (the cabinet suspension), NOT a formal cancellation; GEM's inference-year convention would put the cancelled stamp ~2025. Corroborated by four independent sources (Prachatai, Bangkok Post, Bangkok Tribune, Greenpeace SEA), each carrying 2021 + Chana. Tier set to low to flag the milestone-interpretation caveat (suspension -> inferred cancelled), not because of weak sourcing.

Thailand's third LNG terminal (Gulf MTP LNG Terminal; Gulf 70% / PTT Tank 30%) at Map Ta Phut Industrial Port Phase 3. The Thai cabinet approved the private-entity selection on 24 Sept 2019 and the 35-year PPP with the IEAT was signed in Oct 2019, covering land reclamation plus the Phase-1 LNG terminal (5 Mtpa). 2019 = first public proposal/award of the LNG terminal. Verified via Bangkok Post (Oct 2019 PPP report) and EECO (Eastern Economic Corridor Office government project page), both carrying 2019 + Map Ta Phut.

Phase II = the expansion of the MTP3 LNG terminal toward the planned 10.8 Mtpa total (initial Phase 1 was 5 Mtpa, expandable to 10.8). The two-stage/expandable plan was defined in the 2019 cabinet approval + PPP, so the proposal year for Phase II is also 2019. Same verified sources as Phase I (Bangkok Post Oct 2019 PPP; EECO government page), both carrying 2019 + Map Ta Phut. Tier low because the 2019 sources emphasise Phase 1; treating the 10.8 Mtpa expansion as a distinct Phase-II proposal milestone in 2019 is a judgment (the expansion was part of the original 2019 plan).

Shell/BPL 'gas-to-power' LNG terminal at Clifton Pier (Shell won the BPL bid in 2018; heavy press 2020-2021), which then stalled — described as indefinitely stalled and dropped from Shell's website by ~2023 — before being revived in a new FOCOL/Shell configuration (NPG) in 2025. Could not verify a specific shelving year from an independent source before the session web-tool limit. UNRESOLVED; unverified candidate year ~2022-2023.

AES Ocean Cay / Ocean Express LNG terminal (EIA filed Sept 2002, approved Oct 2003) was repeatedly delayed by local opposition; AES decided to sell/lease the Ocean Cay site to a Bahamian company in Aug 2009 — the effective abandonment (the island later became MSC Cruises' Ocean Cay). Candidate cancellation year 2009, but could not verify a source page that ties 2009 specifically to the abandonment before the session web-tool limit (the offshore-technology / oilandgasadvancement project profiles failed to fetch, and '2009' on such pages may refer to planned construction, which would be a misleading citation). UNRESOLVED pending verification.
